The text contains several specific historical markers that pinpoint its time period. The most definitive clue is the mention of the "ratification of the 18th Amendment." The 18th Amendment to the United States Constitution, which established the prohibition of alcohol, was ratified on January 16, 1919, and went into effect a year later in 1920.

Additionally, the pamphlet advocates for the "prohibition of alcohol" and speaks of the "dangers of the liquor trade." This aligns with the era of Prohibition in the United States, which lasted from 1920 to 1933. The tone of the pamphlet, focusing on sobriety and the negative impacts of the liquor industry, is characteristic of the temperance movement that culminated in the passage of the 18th Amendment.

Therefore, the text dates to the early 1920s, specifically around the time of the ratification of the 18th Amendment in 1919 or shortly thereafter during the initial years of Prohibition.
